clue.text: One cause of decline in the 24: filthy WC, repair needed

definitions.text: One cause of decline in the 24

indicators.note: filthy here suggests the letters are messed up and dirtied into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters W and C

explanation.surface: A grubby public toilet in urgent need of repair, the kind of decay a run-down shopping street shows.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' points to the answer of 24 across, the traditional shopping street; 'filthy' rearranges WC plus REPAIR. 'needed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops slashing prices against each other can drive rivals out of business, one reason a shopping street declines.

clue.text: Before, it was on every 24; after, unavailable, it's frozen

parts.note: post- is the prefix meaning after
a dish that is off the menu is unavailable
ice is frozen water

explanation.surface: A nostalgic sigh about something once on every street that is now unavailable and stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' belongs to the definition, nodding to how common these were; 'after' starts the wordplay. 'every 24' means every high street.
explanation.definitionFit: Branches handling mail and pensions used to be found on every British shopping street, many since closed.

clue.text: Make stronger source of protein more pricey?

parts.note: beef is meat, a source of protein
prices that are up have risen, so dearer

explanation.surface: A shopper grumbling that meat has become dearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb meaning to reinforce or strengthen something, as in bolstering security.

clue.text: Shut down empty bakery, conveniently located

parts.note: to close a business is to shut it down

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its shell, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A bakery has closed and stands empty, though it was handily placed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nearby is conveniently located, within easy reach.

clue.text: Set up plans for cheap source of protein

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: Someone drawing up plans to provide inexpensive protein.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinned processed pork luncheon meat, long known as a budget protein.

clue.text: Deception in amusing farce

parts.note: funny means amusing
farce is also forcemeat, a stuffing for meat or poultry

explanation.surface: A farce built on trickery, as comedies so often are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'farce' looks theatrical but is the cookery word for stuffing; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for trickery or underhand behaviour, as in 'no funny business'.

clue.text: Stick to what you'll find in the classifieds?

definitions.text: what you'll find in the classifieds?
definitions.meaning: split as two words, an advert placed here: the small-ads pages are where advertisements are found

explanation.surface: Instructions to keep to what the small-ads pages offer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as 'ad here'. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling or be fixed to a surface, the same as sticking.

clue.text: Wooded area and lake conceal backward-looking rip off

indicators.note: one word concealing another holds it inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: looking backwards means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to rip off is to rob
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A woodland and its lake hiding some backward-looking swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'area' doubles as part of the wordplay; the reversed theft word goes in after AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to trees or living among them, so wooded in a broad adjectival sense.

clue.text: With 26 across, often found quietly replacing leading firms

definitions.text: With 26 across, often found quietly replacing leading firms

indicators.note: one letter replacing another takes its place in the word
leading means the first letter of the word

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Bargain stores have crept in and taken over from the major retailers.
explanation.walkthrough: Combined with 26 across this gives the bargain store; P swaps in for the first letter of 'found', taken from 'firms'.
explanation.definitionFit: Discount stores selling everything for a single coin unit have replaced bigger chains on British streets.

clue.text: Historical payment for spy to remove uniform

indicators.note: removing a letter takes it out of the word

parts.note: a scout spies out the land
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A spy is paid off, historically, for getting rid of a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: An old tax or levy, surviving in the phrase scot-free.

clue.text: Sole trader on the 24?

parts.note: a sole trader is a one-person business, but sole is also a flatfish, so this is someone selling fish on the high street

explanation.surface: A one-person business on the high street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole trader' reads as the business term; the fish is the point.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling fish, sole among them, on a shopping street.

clue.text: Out-of-town supermarket admits responsibility

indicators.note: the letters come out of the following words, which hold them

explanation.surface: An edge-of-town superstore confesses to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb meaning to confess or accept blame.

clue.text: Temporarily transfer worker to grass: it's growing on the 24

parts.note: to second staff is to move them to another post for a time
a hand is a manual worker
to grass is to inform on someone, which is also to shop them

explanation.surface: A boss seconds a worker who then informs on colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'grass' is the informer's verb, not lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity and used-goods stores are a growing presence on British shopping streets.

clue.text: Money man gets parole — at last, free

parts.note: bucks are dollars, money
he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: at last means take the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man with money finally gets parole and walks free.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang of Hindi origin meaning given without charge.

clue.text: How to pay for something from an 11?

definitions.meaning: cash on delivery, a way of paying when goods arrive
a white fish sold by the fish trader of 11 across

explanation.surface: Asking how to pay for something bought from a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation for paying cash on delivery, and a common white fish.

clue.text: Type of apostrophe produced by semi-literate costermonger (not me!) should be deleted

indicators.note: a semi-literate writer jumbles the spelling, so the letters are reordered
these letters are struck out of the larger set before the rest is arranged

explanation.surface: A barrow-boy's sign with a misplaced apostrophe, and the setter insisting he did not write it.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip N, O, T, M, E from COSTERMONGER and rearrange the rest. A costermonger is a street fruit seller.
explanation.definitionFit: The stray apostrophe in signs such as 'apple's', named after shopkeepers who commonly write it.

clue.text: One is on top of recording every foul

definitions.text: One is on top of recording every foul

indicators.note: in a down entry the top of each word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An official who notes every infringement.
explanation.definitionFit: The match official keeps track of every foul committed.

clue.text: Odd? Put a revised total

indicators.note: revised means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about an odd sum, followed by a corrected total.
explanation.definitionFit: To total is to come to a sum, the phrasal verb meaning amount to.

clue.text: No more credit to do minimal business?

parts.note: buying on tick is buying on credit
over means finished, no more

explanation.surface: A shop that ends credit so as to keep trading at a low level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. Tick is British slang for credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for running slowly, like an idling engine, so trading at a low level.

clue.text: Butcher learns a place to keep things that might go off

definitions.text: place to keep things that might go off

indicators.note: to butcher is to mangle or hack up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A butcher learns where to store meat that might spoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' suggests food spoiling, but means weapons firing.
explanation.definitionFit: A store for weapons and ammunition, which might explode.

clue.text: Make good lunch when? Late afternoon, say?

parts.note: lunch is often at one o'clock

indicators.note: say means the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: four o'clock is late afternoon

explanation.surface: Someone apologising for being late, asking when lunch was and offering a late afternoon instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends for a wrong is to make good on it.

clue.text: Boatman changing direction for chemist's last place on the 24

indicators.note: changing one letter for another swaps it

parts.note: a sailor is a boatman; Boatman is also the setter
S is south, a compass direction

indicators.note: last means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: The setter swapping roles for a chemist's shop on the high street.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap S for the T ending 'chemist's'. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes-maker's shop is one of the traditional premises on a shopping street.

clue.text: See 2
"Love, constant, above all" — Boatman's sea creatures

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
top means above all others
the setter is Boatman, so Boatman is I

explanation.surface: The setter's sea creatures, prized above all.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the eight-armed sea animal, so sea creatures.

clue.text: Eminent setter making changes to the traditional marketplace

parts.note: high means lofty, eminent

indicators.note: changes to a word rearrange its letters

explanation.surface: A distinguished setter remodelling the old market square.
explanation.definitionFit: The main shopping street of a British town, traditionally where trade happens.

clue.text: A long walk for Mum going out with market disbanded

indicators.note: going out means these letters leave the larger set
disbanded means broken up, so the remaining letters are reordered

parts.note: ma is mum, mother

explanation.surface: Mum's market has broken up, so she faces a long walk.
explanation.walkthrough: MA leaves MARKET; RKET is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An arduous journey on foot, a long walk.

clue.text: See 13
Criticise half-hearted shopping centres, when erected

indicators.note: in a down entry erected means raised up, written bottom to top
the double letter at the heart is halved, so one is lost

parts.note: malls are shopping centres

explanation.surface: Criticising lukewarm shopping centres when they are built.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam is to criticise harshly.

clue.text: Come back without second part of 9

indicators.note: without means the letter is dropped

parts.note: to bounce is to rebound, come back
B is second, as in a B grade or the second letter

explanation.surface: A return without a second part.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' refers to 9 across, the unit of weight there.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound weight is sixteen of these smaller units.

clue.text: One offers concessions in a shopping centre to wipe out first of retailers to go back

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters
going back means moving the letter towards the end

parts.note: to erase is to wipe out

indicators.note: the first of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Shop owners wiping out retailers in a mall while one makes concessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shopping centre' is PP; the R in ERASE, matching the first letter of 'retailers', moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who placates by giving ground, as in appeasement.
